Jon has a mass of 84 kg. He was at a friend's party and consumed six bottles of an alcoholic beverage, each equivalent to 0.9 standard drinks.

Blood alcohol content ($BAC$) is calculated using the following formula:

$$BAC_{Male} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking, and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Jon stopped drinking at 10:30 pm and left the party at 2:30 am, just when his Blood Alcohol Content ($BAC$) reached zero.

The time needed for $BAC$ to reach zero after the last drink consumed can be calculated using the formula:

$$\text{Number of hours for } BAC \text{ to reach zero} = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$

At what time did Jon start to have his first drink at the party? Give your answer to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex: Answer B. (The handwritten copy shows option B as \$1\,530 with \$1532.50 written beside it.)

$$\dfrac{50}{1.5} = 33.3 \text{ m/s}$$

$$\text{Speed} = \dfrac{33.3 \times 3600}{1000} = 120 \text{ km/h}$$

$\therefore$ over the speed limit

$$4 = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$

$$BAC = 0.06$$

$$0.06 = \dfrac{10 \times 5.4 - 7.5H}{6.8 \times 84}$$

$$H = 2 \text{ h } 38 \text{ min}$$

Drinking started at 7:52 pm.

Smallest value of $x$ is given by the largest angle $41 + 2 = 43^\circ$ and the shortest rope length $16.2 - 0.1 = 16.1$.

$$x = 16.1 \cos 43^\circ = 11.8$$

Largest value of $x$ is given by the smallest angle $41 - 2 = 39^\circ$ and the longest rope length $16.2 + 0.1 = 16.3$.

$$x = 16.3 \cos 39^\circ = 12.7$$

$\therefore$ $11.8$ and $12.7$

notes: Bundled solutions are a scanned, handwritten worked copy (pages 26-52); no marking criteria are given so marks_breakdown is null. Paper typos: Section II header says 'Attempt Questions 11 - 33' but the paper runs to Q36 (cover says 11-36); Q8 'roates' (routes); Q13(a) 'On the cumulative frequency above' (missing 'histogram'); Q34(b) 'deprecation' (depreciation); Q35(b) 'taught' (taut). Q34: printed purchase price is $34 600 but the handwritten solution uses $34 000 (gives 18400 and 3.2%); with $34 600 the answers would be 19 000 and 3.7%; likely the question should read $34 000 - needs a teacher decision. Q6: handwritten key marks B and notes 1532.50; the printed option B is $1 532.50 on the question paper (the solutions copy prints $1 530). Q31: handwritten working uses 9 and 11 days of interest and rate written as '8.5%' (read as 18.5%); the question's 4 April-30 April (27 days) and 13 April-30 April (18 days) would give different values; solution transcribed as written, flagged. Q14 handwriting reads '4x74x60', interpreted as 4x24x60 = 5760. Q28 handwriting calls 7:52 pm the 'last drink' but it is the start time; the question asks for the first drink. Q36(a) handwritten unit 'm^2' should be m^3; 11000 in (b) read as 12000 (942478 = 2*pi*25*12000/2). Q23(a) answer 3.5 only. Q12 'ADEG' only. Q13(b) median 3:50. Q4 solutions copy prints option A as '-0.005 m'. Option figures for Q8 have empty latex with figure_key. Page 27 onward: pages 26 (cover with 'Solutions'), 27 blank; reference sheet pp 25 and 53 skipped. No old_syllabus/standard_topic set (Standard 2 paper).
